text:
maria.chen: heads-up — spotted rows from org-82 showing up in a handful of QuickDash widgets for org-17 during the canary this morning.
kevin: whoa. repro steps?
maria.chen: open quickdash for a user in org-17 -> widget shows 3 rows with org metadata saying org-82 in the small badge. only on canary route (edge-node-7).
sophia: any chance this is telemetry sampling artifact? or the snapshot replay job?
maria.chen: checked logs — request headers looked fine: X-Org-ID=17, session cookie matches. attaching quick log from edge:
```
[edge-node-7] recv request id=abc123 path=/api/quickdash user=alice org=17 route=canary
[edge-node-7] upstream fetch -> dashboard-service-2, cached:view:quickdash:org=82 keyhit
[edge-node-7] returned 200 body(rows=5) metadata.org_hint=82
```
kevin: oh no — edge returned cached view for org=82 even though request header was 17. That suggests our cache key lacks org scoping on that code path.
alex: which cache layer? shared view cache on edge or the dashboard service?
maria.chen: stack trace shows the cache hit was at the edge LRU (view-cache) before the request reached dashboard-service. code path is the prefetch layer we added for canary warmups.
sophia: might be a namespace collision where prefetch uses a temporary tenant key like "global-quickdash" during warmup and we forgot to attach real org id for subsequent lookups.
kevin: can we check the cache key formation? look for missing tenant segment. if the warmup push sets TTL and then the lookup uses fingerprint without org on a fast path, that's the bug.
maria.chen: found the code: prefetch job calls `prefetchQuickDash(org=null, templateId)` when org is unknown for templated warmups. Then downstream lookups call `getView(templateId)` — earlier code assumed templateId alone was safe.
kevin: ugh. so the warmup created a template-scoped cache entry that is serving other tenants. Critical.
alex: mitigation: flush the view-cache on edge-node-7 and disable prefetch warmups until we ship a fix. I can push a rollout. :exclamation:
sophia: also add an assertion to cache key builder to require org id unless the entry is explicitly marked global. We should never mark a tenant-specific UI as global.
maria.chen: quick patch: require org in key or add suffix `:global` when intended. I'll open a canary PR.
kevin: ops action: alex, please run `edge-cache flush --node edge-node-7 --pattern quickdash*` and revert canary routing for that node.
alex: doing now. `/edgectl flush edge-node-7 quickdash*` -> deploy-bot: started job 8921.

[deploy-bot] job 8921: in progress
[deploy-bot] job 8921: completed OK (flushed 42 keys)

alex: rolled canary off edge-node-7 for route quickdash. traffic diverted to stable nodes.
sophia: good. next steps: maria send PR for key fix + test, kevin add postmortem blurb to the incident board, and add an integration test that warms up prefetch and asserts subsequent lookups include org segment.
maria.chen: on it — will include reproducer script. also adding a short telemetry metric: cache_hit_org_mismatch count when cached metadata.org_hint != request org.
kevin: +1 for metric. helps detect if similar leak shows up elsewhere.
kevin: estimate rollout fix in ~2 hours?
maria.chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dashboard/compare/patch/prefetch-org-key-fix (wip).
alex: thanks. logging this thread into eng-platform incident tracker. :thumbsup:
kevin: postmortem once PR lands and we verify no further leaks. small customer impact — reached out to CS to surface to affected orgs.
maria.chen: noted. thanks all.
